title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Spiced rice with salmon, soft-boiled eggs, and peas
excerpt: Kedgeree arrived in Britain via the Indian subcontinent during the colonial period, adapted from the rice and lentil dish khichdi. Smoked haddock is traditional, but salmon works very well and is easier to source. The combination of warm spices, flaky fish, and soft egg yolk is as good for a late breakfast as it is for a light supper.
sourceNotes: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish derived from the South Asian khichdi, a simple rice and lentil preparation. British colonists adapted it in the 19th century using smoked fish, hard-boiled eggs, and curry powder, and it became a popular Victorian breakfast dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The rice can be cooked a day ahead and refrigerated. Reheat in the pan with a splash of water.

content.text: Fold the salmon in gently at the end to keep the flakes large. Stirring too vigorously breaks the fish down into small shreds.

items.prepNote: skin on (smoked haddock is traditional and works equally well)
hard-boiled for 7 minutes, then peeled and quartered

content.text: Bring a wide pan of salted water to a gentle simmer. Add the salmon skin-side down and poach for 8 minutes until the flesh is just cooked through and flakes easily. Lift out and flake into large pieces, discarding the skin and any bones.

Cook the rice in the large saucepan with 600 ml of salted water. Bring to the boil, then reduce to the lowest possible heat, cover tightly, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to steam, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked rice to the spiced onion pan and stir to combine. Add the frozen peas and stir over medium heat for 2 minutes until the peas are heated through.
Gently fold in the flaked salmon and the quartered eggs. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter the chopped parsley over the top and serve with lemon wedges on the side.

items.cause: Too much water, or the lid was lifted during cooking
items.fix: Use the 2:1 water-to-rice ratio and resist lifting the lid for at least 12 minutes.

items.symptom: The egg yolks are fully hard rather than jammy
items.fix: Boil for exactly 7 minutes, then transfer to cold water immediately. 7 minutes gives a set but still creamy yolk.
